nodes.title: Data Union Conference
nodes.tldr: Data Union Conference Anonymous (not verified) Fri, 09/18/2026 - 09:43   12 January 2027   Charlemagne building, Brussels, Belgium Bringing policymakers, businesses, expe...
nodes.details: Data Union Conference Anonymous (not verified) Fri, 09/18/2026 - 09:43   12 January 2027   Charlemagne building, Brussels, Belgium Bringing policymakers, businesses, experts and researchers together to turn Europe’s data policies into more data for AI, growth and competitiveness. This high-level conference will be hosted by the European Commission. It will contribute to a wider political debate on the future of the EU data Policy. Main topics on the agenda During the conference, discussions will focus on: Digital Omnibus: Simplifying the EU data rulebook, reducing administrative burden and supporting innovation Data for industrial AI: Improving access to high-quality data through the Data Act International data flows: Promoting open and trusted data flows and securing fair treatment for EU companies abroad The agenda will be published here. Register You can express your interest in participating. Admission is subject to approval. The event is going to be live streamed. Background European companies and researchers need better access to high-quality data to develop and deploy AI. The Data Union Strategy sets out practical measures to increase data availability and strengthen Europe’s data infrastructure. The Commission is also working to simplify the EU’s digital rules. Building on the Data Act and other existing legislation, the aim is to reduce unnecessary burdens and make it easier for companies to use and share data. Internationally, the Commission seeks to facilitate trusted cross-border data flows and address unfair restrictions faced by EU companies in other markets. Together, these efforts aim to support AI development and strengthen Europe’s competitiveness. Organiser European Commission Express your interest in participating Related topics Big data Data policy Open data Artificial intelligence

nodes.title: EU KIDS Act to restrict social media platforms’ access to children in the EU
nodes.tldr: EU KIDS Act to restrict social media platforms’ access to children in the EU Anonymous (not verified) Thu, 09/17/2026 - 09:36 The European Commission has adopted the EU KIDS Act to...
nodes.details: EU KIDS Act to restrict social media platforms’ access to children in the EU Anonymous (not verified) Thu, 09/17/2026 - 09:36 The European Commission has adopted the EU KIDS Act to enhance the online safety of children throughout the Union. The proposal prohibits social media platforms from accessing children under the age of 13 and sets an EU-wide minimum age for minors to open an account of their own at the age of 15, thereby ensuring a gradual approach. The KIDS Act also reverses the burden of proof. Now, service providers will have to show that their services are age-appropriate and safe by design. Commission President, Ursula von der Leyen, said: “Today, our children are engaging with the most sophisticated technologies ever created. Technology that was never created with their wellbeing in mind. Our KIDS Act is reversing the burden of proof - it is for platforms to show they are safe by design. And we put parents back in the driving seat, giving them the tools to help their children navigate a safer online world.” Read the full press release and factsheet. Find further information: Kids Act - Proposal and supporting documents KIDS Act - questions and answers Related topics Better Internet for Children Strengthening trust and security Online platforms and e-commerce Related content Policy and legislation17 September 2026Proposal for EU KIDS Act - 'EU Keeping Internet Digital Spaces Accountable and Trustworthy'This proposal seeks to protect minors from risky digital services and AI systems, uphold the digital single market and maintain a coherent regulatory framework and enforcement structure for the protection of minors online.

nodes.title: Proposal for EU KIDS Act - 'EU Keeping Internet Digital Spaces Accountable and Trustworthy'
nodes.tldr: Proposal for EU KIDS Act - 'EU Keeping Internet Digital Spaces Accountable and Trustworthy' Anonymous (not verified) Thu, 09/17/2026 - 09:21 This proposal seeks to protect minors f...
nodes.details: Proposal for EU KIDS Act - 'EU Keeping Internet Digital Spaces Accountable and Trustworthy' Anonymous (not verified) Thu, 09/17/2026 - 09:21 This proposal seeks to protect minors from risky digital services and AI systems, uphold the digital single market and maintain a coherent regulatory framework and enforcement structure for the protection of minors online. The proposal recognises the risks that minors face on certain online social networking services and video-sharing platforms and therefore limits autonomous account creation on those specific platforms and systems by children below the age of 15 years. By providing one age across the European Union, it harmonises diverging national rules removing obstacles to the implementation of the Digital Single Market, ensuring legal certainty and a similar level of protection for all children in the European Union. The proposal and its supporting documents are available on EUR-Lex and will soon be accessible in all official EU languages: Proposal for EU KIDS Act - 'EU Keeping Internet Digital Spaces Accountable and Trustworthy' Communication accompanying the KIDS Act - An EU approach to online child safety Staff Working Document (SWD) - Analysis of Impacts accompanying the proposal for EU kids Act Provide your feedback to the consultation on the EU KIDS ACT until 26 November 2026 (midnight Brussels time).
